```{r}
#| include: false
# Slides for the "Demographic Divides" resource page: one question per
# demographic group, as weighted shares from the cvpa R package.
#
# Render from the repository root with:
#   bash site/scripts/render_slides.sh

library(cvpa)
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 6.1, fig.height = 2.8, out.width = "\\linewidth",
                      fig.align = "center", dev = "pdf")

# one question per demographic group, and the response plotted
slides <- tribble(
  ~title,             ~question,       ~response,      ~group_var,
  "Gender",           "bri_soim_012",  "Yes",          "gender",
  "Age",              "bri_soim_011",  "Favour",       "age_cats",
  "Education",        "bri_idim_007",  "Agree",        "degree",
  "Language",         "bri_intd_008",  "Continue",     "language",
  "Region",           "gal_soim_006",  "Favour",       "region",
  "Religion",         "bri_soim_005",  "Always legal", "religion",
  "Union membership", "bri_econ_003",  "Too much",     "union_household",
  "Community size",   "bri_idim_011",  "Agree",        "com_100"
)

# the groups compared for each grouping variable: the package's category
# names, and the shorter labels shown on the slides
group_labels <- list(
  gender          = c("Woman" = "Woman", "Man" = "Man"),
  age_cats        = c("18-29" = "18–29", "30-49" = "30–49", "50+" = "50+"),
  degree          = c("University Degree" = "Degree", "No University Degree" = "No degree"),
  language        = c("French" = "French", "English" = "English"),
  region          = c("Atlantic" = "Atlantic", "Quebec" = "Quebec", "Ontario" = "Ontario",
                      "Prairies" = "Prairies", "British Columbia" = "BC"),
  religion        = c("None" = "No religion", "Catholic" = "Catholic", "Protestant" = "Protestant"),
  union_household = c("Union Member in Household" = "Union",
                      "No Union Member in Household" = "Non-union"),
  com_100         = c("Population > 100k" = "Over 100,000", "Population <= 100k" = "Under 100,000")
)

update_cvpa_data(questions = slides$question, quiet = TRUE)
catalog <- question_catalog()

# colours: ordered groups (age) get one hue from light to dark; others get
# distinct hues in a fixed order
categorical <- c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#e87ba4")
sequential  <- c("#86b6ef", "#2a78d6", "#104281")

latex_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\textbackslash{}", x)
  x <- gsub("([&%$#_{}])", "\\\\\\1", x)
  x <- gsub("~", "\\\\textasciitilde{}", x)
  x <- gsub('"([^"]*)"', "``\\1''", x)
  x
}

slide_data <- function(question, response, group_var, groups) {
  d <- question_data(question)
  n <- d %>%
    filter(!is.na(response), !is.na(.data[[group_var]])) %>%
    count(year, group = .data[[group_var]])
  wtd_response(d, grouping_vars = group_var) %>%
    rename(group = all_of(group_var)) %>%
    filter(response == !!response, group %in% names(groups)) %>%
    left_join(n, by = c("year", "group")) %>%
    filter(n >= 75) %>%
    mutate(group = factor(groups[as.character(group)], levels = groups))
}

# spread label positions apart so no two are closer than `gap`, keeping
# them as close as possible to where the lines end
spread_labels <- function(y, gap = 0.065) {
  o <- order(y); z <- y[o]
  for (k in seq_along(z)[-1]) z[k] <- max(z[k], z[k - 1] + gap)
  over <- max(0, z[length(z)] - 1)          # shift down if pushed past 100%
  z <- z - over
  for (k in rev(seq_along(z))[-1]) z[k] <- min(z[k], z[k + 1] - gap)
  y[o] <- z
  y
}

slide_plot <- function(dat, colours) {
  span <- range(dat$year)
  ends <- dat %>%
    group_by(group) %>%
    filter(year == max(year)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(label_x = span[2] + diff(span) * 0.025,
           label_y = spread_labels(response_share))
  ggplot(dat, aes(year, response_share, colour = group)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(size = 1.6) +
    # each line is labelled just past its last point, in place of a legend
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = group),
              hjust = 0, size = 3.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = function(l) { b <- scales::breaks_pretty(6)(span); b[b >= span[1] & b <= span[2]] },
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.2))) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_text(colour = "grey35"),
          plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 2, 2))
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
for (i in seq_len(nrow(slides))) {
  s <- slides[i, ]
  groups <- group_labels[[s$group_var]]
  dat <- slide_data(s$question, s$response, s$group_var, groups)
  colours <- if (s$group_var == "age_cats") sequential else categorical[seq_along(groups)]
  names(colours) <- groups
  wording <- catalog$question_wording[catalog$question == s$question]

  cat("\n\n## ", s$title, ": ", latex_escape(catalog$issue_label[catalog$question == s$question]), "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("```{=latex}\n{\\footnotesize\\color{wording} ", latex_escape(wording),
      " \\textit{Weighted share answering ``", latex_escape(s$response), "''.}",
      " (\\texttt{", latex_escape(s$question), "})\\par}\n\\vspace{0.3em}\n```\n\n", sep = "")
  print(slide_plot(dat, colours))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## More to explore

\vspace{1em}

These slides show one question for each demographic group, from the Canadian Voting and Policy Attitudes dataset. Figures are weighted shares of respondents, computed with the `cvpa` R package, for years in which each group has at least 75 respondents. Points are survey years; where the line crosses a long gap, no surveys asked the question in between.

\vspace{1em}

For more questions to explore, and for the data, the interactive app, and the R package, visit **policyattitudes.ca/resources**.
